Published online:
    10 September 2026

Geographic focus:
    North America — United States (Rhode Island, Pennsylvania, PJM Interconnection region / Mid-Atlantic, New England)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [NO]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [NO]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — deal closures expected Q1 2027; structural demand shift from data centers ongoing

Synopsis:
    Shell is divesting its 609 MW gas-fired RISEC complex in Rhode Island to Constellation Energy for $715M, while simultaneously acquiring 169 MW Hunlock Creek gas generation in Pennsylvania. Both moves are driven by Shell's strategic repositioning within PJM, the largest North American power market, where data center-driven power demand has materially elevated power prices. Constellation gains a foothold in supply-constrained New England. Both transactions pending regulatory approval, expected to close Q1 2027.
